To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Hh signaling molecules are significantly increased in B-CLLL cells and that Hh signaling regulates B-CLL survival.

1) B-CLL is characterized by an increased survival of neoplastic cells due to their increased resistance to apoptosis; 2) B-CLLL cells are in close contact with bone marrow stromal cells, which provide a survival factor(s); 3) the Hh signaling inhibitor cyclopamine inhibits stromal cell– induced survival of B- CLL cells, suggesting that Hh signaling plays a role in the survival of CLL cells; 4) gene expression profiling of
Hh signaling molecules are up-regulated in primary B-CLLL cells and that Hh signaling regulates BCL2 expression in B-CLLL.
